description:
### Finding (TKT-126 post-merge gate, 2026-07-27)

`TestScheduledReleaseIsLazyAndObservable`
(`services/inventory/internal/store/channel_allocations_smoke_test.go:217`) failed once on merged
`main` and passed on an immediate re-run of the **identical tree**:

```
channel_allocations_smoke_test.go:217: public after release: <nil> available=10 want 8 (unsold 4 returned)
```

### Why it is a flake, not a regression

- The same tree passed the gate **before** the merge (`dd4e121`) and **again after** (`ff89e69`,
  second run). `git diff dd4e121 ff89e69` is empty.
- TKT-126 changed **no file** under `services/inventory/internal/store/`.
- The test is wall-clock and DB-clock dependent by construction: it polls `Availability` against a
  10-second deadline waiting to cross `release_at`, with the comment *"Cross release_at by DB time.
  Reads only — no mutation, no sweeper."*

The channel side had already released (`ch.Available == 0` passed); the **public** projection still
read the pre-release figure, so the two derived reads observed different sides of the release
boundary within one test run. That points at the lazy/derived read path being evaluated against a
clock that can move between the two calls, under load.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root-caused: identify why the channel read and the public read can disagree about whether
      `release_at` has been crossed, within one test run.
- [ ] The fix is in the **test's synchronization or the read path**, not a `time.Sleep` bump — a
      longer sleep hides the disagreement rather than removing it.
- [ ] Fails deterministically before the fix (e.g. by pinning or skewing the clock), passes after.
- [ ] If the disagreement is possible in production and not only in the test, say so explicitly and
      link the resulting ticket — a lazy release that two readers see differently is a real
      availability bug, not a test-harness artifact.

### Notes

Same class as TKT-132 (flaky recovery-sweep race). Worth checking whether both share a root cause in
how derived/lazy reads observe a moving boundary.
